title: Resilient ejection policy for dedicated shards with hosted buffering
creator: Ava Thompson
description: Design and implement a resilient ejection policy for dedicated capacity shards that uses a hosted buffering (temporary spillover) layer rather than immediate global fallback. Goal is to minimize customer-visible variance in latency and failure rate during transient dedicated capacity pressure while keeping costs bounded and preserving strong tenant isolation guarantees.
acceptance_criteria: Ejection decision executes within 50ms of capacity event detection for a shard
Requests routed to hosted buffer preserve token-level billing attribution and tenant metadata
Automatic rollback path exists for stall conditions where hosted buffering exceeds cost thresholds
No P0 customer incidents in a 7-day canary run for top-10 tenants after rollout
Dashboard shows ejection counts, buffer fill ratio, and per-tenant latency delta for the last 30 days
technical_notes: We will implement an ejection controller per-region per-shard that computes a short-lived ejection score using: available_slots, recent_queue_latency (p99), active_kv_cache_hitrate, tenant_priority_weight.
Ejection types: soft-eject (probabilistic sampled spill to hosted), hard-eject (stop scheduling to dedicated and require hosted), and prefetch-eject (move pre-warmed slots).
Hosted buffering will accept requests for max 120s per-tenant during events; buffering layer enforces quota and per-tenant backpressure tokens to limit cost exposure.
We must propagate original model_variant and allow hosted to map to compatible quantized variant. Mapping table stored in config service with versioning and fallback chains.
Metrics to emit: shard_eject_attempts, shard_eject_success, buffer_enqueue_ms, buffer_dequeue_ms, buffer_cost_estimated, tenant_latency_delta_p50_p99.
We will reuse the existing arbitration stream (eng: capacity-adjudicator) but extend it with decay windows to avoid flip-flopping under oscillating load.
decisions: Use probabilistic soft-ejection as default to reduce large-scale traffic shifts and allow progressive ramp of hosted traffic.
Hosted buffering limited to 10% of tenant daily token quota by default; can be increased via tenant-specific policies for enterprise customers.
Model variant substitution is allowed only when semantic-compatibility tag matches and regression delta < 2% on quality evals for the tenant's top prompt set.
Circuit-breaker triggers: buffer_cost_estimated exceeds configured budget OR buffer_queue_latency_p99 > 2x dedicated_p99 for > 30s.
Rollback path will demote to per-tenant throttling rather than immediate global failover to preserve isolation.

comments: 2026-02-12 - Ava Thompson: Initial scoping finished. Decided to pursue buffering vs immediate failover after analysis showed ~30% lower request churn in pilot simulation.
2026-02-20 - Diego Morales: Implemented core ejection controller prototype. Observed oscillation in synthetic load test; introduced decay window (15s) to dampen flip-flop.
2026-02-28 - Priya Nair (SRE): Reviewed controller; recommended adding explicit per-tenant budget accounting to avoid noisy neighbor cost spikes. Added to tasks.
2026-03-03 - Rodrigo (Product): Concern about model quality when swapping variants. Agreed to require eval delta checks and tenant opt-in for aggressive variant demotion.
2026-03-08 - Diego Morales: Router PR opened. Still blocked by mapping table API contract change; working with model-onboarding team to finalize compatibility tags.
2026-03-11 - QA: Canary plan updated to include synthetic prompt set derived from top-10 tenants. Failure criteria tightened: any p99 latency regression > 15% flagged for rollback.
2026-03-13 - Ava Thompson: Cost-estimation model added to observability. Early numbers suggest 4-7% increase in hosted spend under high churn, within acceptable threshold for pilot.
notes_for_qa: Run load profile A (bursty spike) and validate no more than 10% of requests route to hosted buffer for any single tenant in first 60s.
Validate billing attribution by replaying 10k requests and ensuring token logs include original tenant and ejection_reason tags.
Simulate model_variant failure and verify router remaps to allowed compatible variant and logs substitution event with variant_version.
Verify dashboards show expected metrics and set alerts for buffer_cost_estimated > 80% of budget
implementation_risks: Mapping table inconsistencies could cause incompatible model swaps; mitigated by conservative default and manual triage flow.
Prolonged buffering may increase hosted spend; mitigation: circuit-breaker and tenant budgets with immediate throttling.
Complexity in observability correlating per-tenant latency across two different execution planes (dedicated vs hosted).
